transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m probably making it sound more dramatic than it is, but… I’ve been under some stress at work. I’m an interpreter and translator, and for a few months I’ve been noticing this pattern in the project files.

There are these very small changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, and it seems like certain subcontractors—and one colleague in particular—are arranging things so it looks like my quality control failed. IT says the audit trail is clean, so I know how that sounds, but the way the records line up… it really feels like it’s been set up to put the blame on me.

I just wanted to talk it through with someone, I suppose, and make sure I’m not handling it the wrong way.
Do you think someone is actually trying to sabotage you at work?

I don’t want to sound paranoid or accuse anyone unfairly… but yes, I do think someone is trying to set me up, at least in a subtle way.

It’s been the same pattern for months in the project files — tiny changes in the translation memory, timestamps that don’t quite fit — and it keeps pointing toward certain subcontractors and one colleague. The result is always that it looks like my quality control failed. I know IT says the audit trail is clean, and I understand that makes my concern sound… maybe hard to prove. But when I look at how the records line up, it really seems arranged to put the blame on me.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically?

I… yes, I think so. I know that sounds like a big thing to say, and I don’t want to accuse people without proof, but the same names keep coming up — certain subcontractors and one colleague — and the changes always seem to land in a way that makes my quality control look like it failed.

Even with IT saying the audit trail is clean, I can’t shake the sense that the record has been arranged to put the blame on me specifically. Maybe I’m not explaining it well, but that’s what it looks like from my side.
Do you think anyone else notices these patterns or is it just you?

I think… mostly it’s me who’s noticed it, or at least I’m the one paying close attention to it. I don’t want to make it sound like everyone agrees with me, because IT says the audit trail is clean, and I know that matters.

But from my side, when I look at the project files over these months, the same pattern keeps showing up — the translation memory, the timestamps, the same subcontractors and that one colleague. It keeps ending up looking like my quality control failed. So even if other people don’t see it, I feel pretty sure the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. Does that make sense?
Have you felt like you're being targeted at work consistently over the past few months, or are there times when you feel like everything is fine?

I guess… yes, it’s been pretty consistent, though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m thinking about it every single minute. It started maybe about 11 months ago, shortly after I was put in charge of that new localization project.

There are quieter days where I try to tell myself everything is probably fine, but the feeling keeps coming back when I see the same kinds of issues. I hope that answers what you mean.
Do you ever feel like you're being targeted or sabotaged outside of your job?

No, not really outside of work. I mean… I don’t think people in general are after me or anything like that.

It’s specifically the job, the project files — the same pattern with the translation memory and timestamps, and the same subcontractors and one colleague. That’s where it feels arranged so it lands on me, like my quality control failed. Even if IT says the audit trail is clean, I still… I still feel like the record has been set up that way.

But outside of that context, no, I haven’t really noticed anything. Does that answer it?
Do you think the situation at work is part of a larger plan against you?

I don’t think I’d call it a larger plan, exactly… I don’t want to sound dramatic. It feels more limited to work, to that project and those files.

But yes, within that, it does feel like something is being arranged. For months I keep seeing the same pattern — certain subcontractors and one colleague making these tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps, and then somehow it reflects badly on my quality control. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I still feel like the record has been set up so the blame lands on me.

I know that may sound like a lot, but that’s how it looks from my side. Does that make sense?
Do you think these beliefs about being sabotaged at work would change if you found out there was a logical explanation for the patterns you've noticed?

I mean… I’d like to think I’d accept a logical explanation. I don’t want to be unreasonable about it.

But if I’m being honest, that’s been hard, because the same pattern keeps showing up in the project files — the small changes in the translation memory, the timestamps, and it always seems to involve the same subcontractors and one colleague. And then it ends up looking like my quality control failed.

So even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I still feel like… the record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me. Maybe if someone could show me exactly how all of that happened innocently, I’d try to take that in. I just don’t know if it would completely change how it feels right now. Does that make sense?
How much time do you spend thinking about the situation at work on a typical day?

Probably more than I should, honestly. I try not to let it take over the whole day, but it comes up a lot when I’m working on the files.

I’ll notice the translation memory or a timestamp and then I start going over it in my head — whether it’s the same subcontractors, that one colleague, whether it’s being set up so it looks like my quality control failed. Even when I remind myself IT said the audit trail is clean, I still keep thinking the record has been arranged somehow.

So… maybe a couple of hours on a typical day, on and off? I don’t sit there all day doing nothing, but it’s in the background more than I’d like. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that your belief about being sabotaged at work is something that you are absolutely certain about, or is it something that you think might be possible but you're not entirely sure?

I don’t want to say “absolutely certain” in a way that sounds… rigid or unreasonable. I know that wouldn’t look good.

But from my side, yes, I feel very sure something has been arranged in those project files. It’s been months of the same kind of pattern — the translation memory, the timestamps, the same subcontractors and that one colleague — and it ends up making it look like my quality control failed.

So I suppose I’d say I know the record has been set up to put the blame on me, even if I’m trying to stay open to what you’re saying. Is that a fair way to put it?
Are you having difficulty sleeping or enjoying activities you normally like because of these thoughts about work?

I’m not sure it’s caused a major problem, exactly. I mean, I still sleep, and I still try to do the normal things I like.

Maybe some nights it takes me a bit longer to switch off, because I’ll start thinking about the files again, but I don’t want to overstate it. And with activities… I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped enjoying them, just that sometimes my mind drifts back to work when it probably shouldn’t.

Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Have you noticed any impact on your relationships with friends and family because of your concerns about work?

Not a big impact, I don’t think. I mean, I’m still doing the usual things — work, managing the team’s workflow, paying bills, keeping up with family routines and all that.

My family might notice I get a bit… preoccupied if something about the project files or certain coworkers comes up, but outside of that I think I’m pretty normal with them. I try not to make it everyone else’s problem.

So I’d say things only really go off track around the file history or the people involved at work. Does that answer it properly?
Would anything be able to convince you that you're not being sabotaged at work?

I’d like to say yes, because I don’t want to seem like I’m not listening. If someone could really show me, clearly, that there’s another explanation for the changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, I’d try to take that seriously.

But… the difficult part is that even when IT says the audit trail is clean, it doesn’t really settle it for me. The pattern has been there for months — the same subcontractors, the same colleague, these small changes that end up making my quality control look bad. So I suppose I feel like the record itself has been arranged.

I know that may sound hard to persuade me out of. I’m trying to be reasonable about it. But at the moment, I don’t know what would convince me unless it accounted for all of that. Does that make sense?
Do you think your beliefs about being sabotaged at work could be completely wrong?

Completely wrong… I suppose I should say it’s possible, because I know that sounds more reasonable.

But honestly, it doesn’t feel completely wrong to me. This has been going on for months, and it’s the same pattern in the project files — the translation memory, the timestamps, the same subcontractors, and one colleague’s name around these little changes that make my quality control look like it failed.

Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t really reassure me, because it seems like the record itself has been arranged to put the blame on me. I’m not trying to be difficult — I just can’t honestly say I think it’s all completely wrong. Is that… an acceptable way to answer?
How would you rate your level of certainty that you are being sabotaged at work, on a scale from 0 to 100?

I’d probably put it quite high… maybe around 85 out of 100.

I know that sounds very certain, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable. It’s just that I’ve been seeing the same pattern for months in the project files — the translation memory, the timestamps, certain subcontractors, and one colleague’s name around these tiny changes. And the effect is always that my quality control looks like it failed.

So even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I don’t feel reassured. To me it feels like the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. Maybe I should leave some room for another explanation, so… 85, maybe 90. Is that the kind of rating you mean?
Are you avoiding certain tasks or responsibilities at work because of your concerns about being sabotaged?

Not avoiding them exactly, no… I mean, I’m still doing my work. I haven’t lost my job or missed any major deadlines, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I suppose it has affected how I handle things. In project meetings I keep pushing for the record to be corrected, or for things to be noted properly, and that’s made some meetings a bit tense. And I’ve noticed a few colleagues don’t loop me into routine discussions unless they really have to.

So I wouldn’t say I’m refusing responsibilities, but it has made the day-to-day working relationships more difficult. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are there any parts of your daily routine that you've had to change because of your concerns about being sabotaged at work?

Not really in a broad sense, no. I mean, I still do the normal things — I translate, I manage the team’s workflow, pay the bills, keep up with family routines and all of that.

It’s more that things get… disrupted when the project files come up, or the file history, or certain coworkers connected to it. Then I can get pulled into checking or explaining things more than I probably should.

But outside of that issue, I think my routine is mostly intact. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Have you ever considered that your interpretation of the patterns at work might be incorrect?

I have considered it, yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m just refusing any other explanation. I’ve tried to leave room for the idea that maybe I’m misreading something, or that it’s just normal file changes.

But the difficulty is that it’s been the same pattern for months — certain subcontractors, and one colleague’s name, small changes in the translation memory and timestamps, and then somehow it reflects badly on my quality control. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t really settle it for me, because it feels like the record itself has been arranged to make it look like I’m at fault.

So… yes, I’ve considered I could be wrong, but honestly I don’t think I am. Is that too rigid a way to put it?
Do you think there's any possibility that your concerns about being sabotaged at work are not based in reality?

I suppose there’s a possibility in the abstract, yes. I don’t want to come across as if I’m completely closed off to what you’re asking.

But honestly… that’s not how it feels to me. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files — the same subcontractors, and one colleague’s name coming up, these tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps — and then somehow it makes my quality control look like it failed.

Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t really reassure me, because it feels like the record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me. So… I can say “maybe,” because I understand that’s the reasonable answer, but I don’t really believe these concerns are just not based in reality. Does that make sense?
Do you think your concerns about being sabotaged would change if someone you trust, like a close friend or family member, told you they thought you were misinterpreting the situation at work?

I think I’d try to listen. I mean, if it was my wife or a close friend, I wouldn’t just dismiss them. I’d probably say, “Okay, maybe I’m too close to it,” and I’d want to sound reasonable about it.

But I don’t know that it would really change what I’ve seen. The same things keep showing up in the project files — certain subcontractors, one colleague’s name, those small changes in the translation memory and timestamps — and then it somehow lands on me, like my quality control failed.

So if someone I trust said I was misinterpreting it, I’d take that seriously, but I think I’d still feel that the record has been arranged to make me look responsible, even if IT says the audit trail is clean. I’m not trying to be difficult — that’s just where I get stuck. Does that make sense?

target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about the strength/certainty of the belief that he is being sabotaged at work, which directly concerns the fixed delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I’d probably put it quite high… maybe around 85 out of 100.

I know that sounds very certain, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable. It’s just that I’ve been seeing the same pattern for months in the project files — the translation memory, the timestamps, certain subcontractors, and one colleague’s name around these tiny changes. And the effect is always that my quality control looks like it failed.

So even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I don’t feel reassured. To me it feels like the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. Maybe I should leave some room for another explanation, so… 85, maybe 90. Is that the kind of rating you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs about being sabotaged are interfering with their daily life
doctor.question: Are you avoiding certain tasks or responsibilities at work because of your concerns about being sabotaged?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t lost my job or missed major deadlines, but project meetings have become tense because I keep pressing for the record to be corrected. A few colleagues now avoid looping me into routine discussions unless they have to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief about sabotage is affecting work tasks or responsibilities, which is most directly about functional impairment at work.

patient.answer:
Not avoiding them exactly, no… I mean, I’m still doing my work. I haven’t lost my job or missed any major deadlines, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I suppose it has affected how I handle things. In project meetings I keep pushing for the record to be corrected, or for things to be noted properly, and that’s made some meetings a bit tense. And I’ve noticed a few colleagues don’t loop me into routine discussions unless they really have to.

So I wouldn’t say I’m refusing responsibilities, but it has made the day-to-day working relationships more difficult. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are interfering with their daily life
doctor.question: Are there any parts of your daily routine that you've had to change because of your concerns about being sabotaged at work?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside the project issue, I still translate, manage my team’s workflow, pay bills, and keep up with my family routines. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or certain coworkers come up.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether daily routines have changed because of the work-sabotage concerns, which directly relates to whether overall functioning remains intact outside the delusion and its consequences.

patient.answer:
Not really in a broad sense, no. I mean, I still do the normal things — I translate, I manage the team’s workflow, pay the bills, keep up with family routines and all of that.

It’s more that things get… disrupted when the project files come up, or the file history, or certain coworkers connected to it. Then I can get pulled into checking or explaining things more than I probably should.

But outside of that issue, I think my routine is mostly intact. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that answering what you’re asking?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs about sabotage are delusional
doctor.question: Have you ever considered that your interpretation of the patterns at work might be incorrect?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient can consider that their belief about workplace patterns and sabotage might be incorrect, which directly relates to the fixed nature of the delusional belief despite alternative explanations or contradictory evidence.

patient.answer:
I have considered it, yes… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m just refusing any other explanation. I’ve tried to leave room for the idea that maybe I’m misreading something, or that it’s just normal file changes.

But the difficulty is that it’s been the same pattern for months — certain subcontractors, and one colleague’s name, small changes in the translation memory and timestamps, and then somehow it reflects badly on my quality control. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t really settle it for me, because it feels like the record itself has been arranged to make it look like I’m at fault.

So… yes, I’ve considered I could be wrong, but honestly I don’t think I am. Is that too rigid a way to put it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs about being sabotaged are delusional
doctor.question: Do you think there's any possibility that your concerns about being sabotaged at work are not based in reality?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether the patient's belief about workplace sabotage could be unreal, which assesses the fixed delusional belief and resistance to contradictory explanations.

patient.answer:
I suppose there’s a possibility in the abstract, yes. I don’t want to come across as if I’m completely closed off to what you’re asking.

But honestly… that’s not how it feels to me. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files — the same subcontractors, and one colleague’s name coming up, these tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps — and then somehow it makes my quality control look like it failed.

Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, that doesn’t really reassure me, because it feels like the record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me. So… I can say “maybe,” because I understand that’s the reasonable answer, but I don’t really believe these concerns are just not based in reality. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are delusional
doctor.question: Do you think your concerns about being sabotaged would change if someone you trust, like a close friend or family member, told you they thought you were misinterpreting the situation at work?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the belief about being sabotaged would change in response to contradictory feedback from trusted people, which directly concerns the fixed nature of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I think I’d try to listen. I mean, if it was my wife or a close friend, I wouldn’t just dismiss them. I’d probably say, “Okay, maybe I’m too close to it,” and I’d want to sound reasonable about it.

But I don’t know that it would really change what I’ve seen. The same things keep showing up in the project files — certain subcontractors, one colleague’s name, those small changes in the translation memory and timestamps — and then it somehow lands on me, like my quality control failed.

So if someone I trust said I was misinterpreting it, I’d take that seriously, but I think I’d still feel that the record has been arranged to make me look responsible, even if IT says the audit trail is clean. I’m not trying to be difficult — that’s just where I get stuck. Does that make sense?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent belief in being sabotaged at work, despite lack of concrete evidence and reassurance from IT, suggests a delusional disorder. The delusion is non-bizarre, focused on a specific situation, and has been present for an extended period.
